clue.text: Academy briefly make fun of pathetic fool

blocks.note: an academy is a school, and SCH is its short form
to mock is to make fun of

explanation.surface: Someone at an academy, in short, jeers at a hopeless idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' does not cut a word here; it asks for the standard abbreviation of a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmock is a variant of schmuck, Yiddish-derived slang for a contemptible or foolish person.

clue.text: Junior teacher, might one suppose? Somewhat restrained formerly

blocks.note: sub means under or lesser, as in a junior post
pupils call a woman teacher Miss

explanation.surface: A guess that a substitute teacher might be fairly meek.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the whimsy: a submiss would be a junior miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Submiss is an archaic word for submissive or humble, so rather restrained in manner.

clue.text: Soft drink, one taken after depression

blocks.note: a col is a dip between mountain peaks
a means one

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink, one dose taken after feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low spirits; it is a hollow in a ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola is a sweet carbonated beverage, a typical non-alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Male binding bird by way of thin cord

indicators.note: binding something wraps it round, so one word is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
an ousel is a blackbird
in as in 'in passing', by way of

explanation.surface: A man ties up a bird with fine string.
explanation.definitionFit: Houseline is a small three-stranded nautical line used for seizing.

clue.text: 'Black' (offensive) used in colloquialism, untutored

indicators.note: the letters wanted are used within the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A comment that an offensive term for black people belongs in untutored slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Muntu is a Bantu word for a person, used in South Africa as an offensive term for a black African.

clue.text: Part of shell structure — study feature primed with runny oil

indicators.note: a runny substance flows and loses its shape, so the letters lose their order
something primed with a charge has it loaded inside

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
the chin is a facial feature
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A materials scientist's note on a shell component treated with thin oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell structure' suggests an artillery shell being primed; it is a mollusc's shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Conchiolin is the protein that forms the organic framework of mollusc shells.

clue.text: Gap-filler in (fleeting) fashion? Scotch preferred

indicators.note: one item placed in another means the first sits inside the second

blocks.note: a fad is a short-lived fashion
a hesitation noise used to fill a gap in speech

explanation.surface: A wondering aside about whether a stopgap is just a passing trend, with a Scottish preference noted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' marks the definition as a Scots word, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Faurd is the Scots form of favoured, and being favoured means being preferred.

clue.text: Dandy holding on to antique shoe appendage

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so the first word encloses the rest

blocks.note: a fop is a dandy
re means on or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dandy clinging to an old-fashioned shoe accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On to' looks like a single preposition, but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a foretop was a raised projecting piece at the front of an old-fashioned shoe.

clue.text: Desert dunes? There's a sense of sad loss with soak absent

indicators.note: absent means missing, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
regret is sorrow over something lost
to ret is to soak flax or hemp

explanation.surface: Sorrow felt in a dry desert where nothing can be soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers a loose definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Areg is the plural of erg, a sand-dune region of the Sahara.

clue.text: Nothing in arrêt moved court to apply to the past

indicators.note: one piece placed in the other sits inside it
letters that are moved are shifted into a different order

blocks.note: O looks like zero
taken as written, accent dropped
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A court decision, an arrêt with nothing in it, was moved to have backdated effect.
explanation.walkthrough: An arrêt is a French court's judgment, which fits the legal surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To retroact is to operate retrospectively, taking effect on events already past.

clue.text: Not a bowler's wicket? Worry about that — this team member's vicious!

indicators.note: one word goes about, that is around, the other

blocks.note: to dog is to worry or pester
a run out is a wicket not credited to the bowler; RO is its scorebook abbreviation

explanation.surface: A cricket worry about dismissals, ending with a nasty teammate.
explanation.walkthrough: A droog is a gang member in A Clockwork Orange, hence 'vicious'. In cricket a run out counts as a wicket but not one the bowler takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A droog is a member of a gang, a team of thugs, from Anthony Burgess's invented slang.

clue.text: Not working (10, three words)

blocks.note: surface reading: broken, out of action
setter's reading: just the definition, since this is the word solvers write their own clues for

explanation.walkthrough: This was the Azed competition word: the puzzle gives only a definition, and entrants submit their own clues for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that has broken down and cannot be used carries a sign with this phrase on it.

clue.text: Mull, according to the locals? Some nonsense about loch

indicators.note: one word goes about, that is around, the other

blocks.note: bunk is nonsense
L is the map abbreviation for loch

explanation.surface: Islanders on Mull, it seems, talk nonsense about their loch.
explanation.walkthrough: Mull looks like the Scottish island, which the loch supports, but it is the verb to mull, to bungle; 'according to the locals' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunk is a Scots verb meaning to spoil or mismanage, as to mull something is to make a mess of it.

clue.text: Topers'll get drunk thus?

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry guess at how fast heavy drinkers will become intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the drinkers' name rearranged gives the speed at which they get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto means quickly, as in a musical direction or 'hey presto', the speed at which hard drinkers get tipsy.

clue.text: Distraught over pupil's driving

indicators.note: distraught means deeply agitated, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher upset about a student's driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' looks like motoring but is the adjective for pushing forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Propulsive means tending to propel, pushing forward, which is what a driving force does.

clue.text: Mark a length of timber cut for gum resin

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
taken as written
a stick is a length of wood

explanation.surface: Instructions for marking and cutting wood, perhaps to get at the sap.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin from the lentisk tree, used in varnish and chewing gum.

clue.text: 'Customers right', refrain among heads of chain-store enterprise

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters
pieces that are among others sit between them

blocks.note: its first letter
a lien is a legal right over property
a tag is a refrain or catchphrase
its first letter

explanation.surface: A store chain's slogan that the customer is right, used as a jingle.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'Customers right' looks like a motto, but splits into the definition and a piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Clientage means a body of clients, the customers of a business taken together.

clue.text: Lassie's to assume a married alias: Balm of Gilead?

blocks.note: a Scots girl would say tak for take, to assume
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for married
aka stands for also known as

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl taking a married name, then asking about a biblical balm.
explanation.walkthrough: A lassie is a Scots girl, which marks a Scots form; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Takamaka is a tropical tree yielding a fragrant resin, one of the trees called balm of Gilead.

clue.text: Malleable old fool wielded cloth in wet place

indicators.note: something wielded is swung about, so its letters are thrown into a new order
the reworked letters are put inside the place word

blocks.note: a sog is a soggy, boggy spot
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pliable old idiot flaps a rag about in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: SOG goes around the rearranged letters, after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot-clog was an archaic term for a gullible companion tolerated only because he paid the bill, a dupe easily led.

clue.text: One in blue, but appearing regularly in scarlet?

indicators.note: appearing at regular intervals means taking every other letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A colour joke: someone dressed in blue who keeps turning up in red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour to contrast with scarlet, but the one in blue is a sailor in naval uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an experienced sailor, and navy uniforms are blue.

clue.text: Pole in difficulty producing old dagger

blocks.note: Po. is a dictionary abbreviation for Pole or Polish
taken as written
ado is trouble or difficulty

explanation.surface: A Polish man in trouble pulls an antique knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but here it just strings along.
explanation.definitionFit: Poinado is an obsolete form of poniard, a small slender dagger.

clue.text: Platform's humourless face

blocks.note: as in po-faced, solemn and humourless
dial is slang for the face

explanation.surface: A platform's stony, unsmiling face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Platform's' is possessive in the surface but works as an adjective, 'of a platform'.
explanation.definitionFit: Podial is the adjective from podium, a raised platform, so it means relating to a platform.

clue.text: Playing e.g. L. Hoad he wouldn't have a clue

indicators.note: playing about with the letters puts them in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis remark that a player such as Lew Hoad would be clueless at playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Lew Hoad was an Australian tennis champion of the 1950s; 'Playing' suits him but rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A loghead is a blockhead, a stupid person who is clueless.

clue.text: Sort of snowmobile like this grips child getting on briefly

indicators.note: to grip something is to hold it inside, so one word encloses the other
briefly means shortened, so the word drops its final letter

blocks.note: so means in this way
a kid is a child
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snowmobile type that a child clings to, climbing aboard quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Skidoo is a trade name that came to mean a motorized sledge, a kind of snowmobile.

clue.text: Loose covers will be seen to keep this dry

indicators.note: the words are said to keep, that is to hold within them, the letters wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Advice that loose dust-sheets will keep something dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Seco is the Spanish word for dry, used of sherry and other wines.

clue.text: Chap having to work with a head covering

blocks.note: a chap is a man
to till is to work the soil
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who has to go to work wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To work' looks like going to a job, but it is the farming verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantilla is a lace or silk scarf worn over the head and shoulders by Spanish women.

clue.text: Comfortable sum cunningly invested in well!

indicators.note: done cunningly means artfully reworked, so the letters are reordered
money invested in something is put inside it

blocks.note: my! is an exclamation like well!
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A comfortable sum shrewdly placed in a well, an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comfortable sum' looks like a single phrase, but 'Comfortable' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumsy describes something homely and cosy, unfashionably comfortable.

clue.text: Chow may end up in this batter

definitions.text: Chow may end up in this

blocks.clueFragment: Chow may end up in this
blocks.note: first meaning: an enclosure for stray dogs, a chow being a breed of dog
second meaning: to beat hard and repeatedly

explanation.surface: Food may end up in a cake mix.
explanation.walkthrough: Chow seems to be food and batter cake mix, but chow is a dog breed and batter the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is where stray animals are kept, and to pound is to beat heavily.

clue.text: See Women in Love for this alcoholic

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for women
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A tip to watch the film Women in Love for a portrait of a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Women in Love is the D. H. Lawrence novel and film, but the title is taken apart word by word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is a habitual drinker of cheap wine, an alcoholic down on his luck.

clue.text: Lucky thing ma got rid of children's mark on ground

indicators.note: getting rid of something means discarding it, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: a mascot is a lucky charm
the letters to be discarded, taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: A mother threw away her lucky charm, and the children's mark is left on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'children's mark on ground' read with CH taken from it: a scotch is the line scratched for hopscotch.
explanation.definitionFit: A scotch is a line scored on the ground, as for hopscotch.

clue.text: Age lost in use of derricks for some fish newly landed

indicators.note: something lost is no longer there, so those letters drop out

blocks.note: the noun for employing hoists or derricks, or the fee charged for it
the letters to be removed, taken as written

explanation.surface: Years pass as derricks are used to unload a fresh catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A cran is a measure of freshly landed herrings, about 750 fish.

clue.text: Early Catholic hymn, half cut but with melody included

indicators.note: cutting a word in half leaves only part of it, here its back half
something included is placed inside the other part

blocks.note: taken as written, then halved
an aria is a song or melody

explanation.surface: A hymn of the early Church, abridged but with its tune kept in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half cut' suggests tipsy; here it removes the first half of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Marian was a supporter of the Catholic Mary Tudor or Mary Queen of Scots in the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Brendan's fellow was such a conventional type, without front

definitions.note: an adjective: the fellow was of this kind

indicators.note: having no front means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person

explanation.surface: Brendan's friend was a strait-laced sort who had no front.
explanation.walkthrough: Brendan is Brendan Behan, whose play is The Quare Fellow; the surface makes his fellow sound conventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Quare is an Irish dialect form of queer, odd or strange, as in Behan's title.

clue.text: Vocalize about Group Four's underwater activity (10, two words)

indicators.note: the first word goes about, that is around, the rest

blocks.note: to sing is to vocalize
a kind is a group or class
Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: Talk about a quartet's plans to go swimming underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin diving is swimming underwater with mask and flippers but no diving suit.

clue.text: Derisive utterance about nothing a boy deflected

indicators.note: something deflected is turned aside from its course, so the letters move out of order
the reworked letters go about, that is around, the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A jeer about nothing, aimed at a boy and turned aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Yah-boo or ya-boo is an interjection of mockery and contempt.

clue.text: Blind alley without vegetation skirting pit (7, two words)

indicators.note: to skirt something is to run round its edge, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: land with no growing plants is dead
